checks.name: A priority recheck SQL failure cannot strand an untracked running lease at shutdown
Two blocked books run together while a third file waits for a real slot
Foreground demand fills an unused slot without restarting a background book
Full queue preempts one background book for foreground work without cancelling its peer
Lower resource allowance drains existing work and serializes later admissions
Recovery pages past live owners and restores all 201 orphaned claims
Demand for active background resource revokes lease and persists priority once
Material queue action rejects paths, forged schema, unknown action and stale-shaped IDs
Background queue leaves historical placeholder tasks untouched until explicit adoption
Default parsing is FIFO on the same existing task IDs
Explicit priority interrupts owned background work and resumes it after the target
Teacher cancel prevents running work from committing; explicit retry is once-only
Cancelled queued work stays cancelled through a consumer restart
Source version mismatch is refused both at admission and before parsing
Parse failure remains visible and does not retry endlessly
Shutdown requeues interrupted work and a new consumer resumes it without partial commit
Dead owner recovery never steals a live process claim
Two consumers use SQLite CAS so only one owner enters parsing
Malformed owned payload is quarantined and cannot be adopted as a legacy task
Priority admission before consumer startup runs first without another Agent
Bounded queue views still expose a selected task beyond 100 rows; stop-all drains all batches
Pi waiting is lease-bound and never silently adopts an old placeholder task
A full batch of malformed jobs is quarantined without starving valid later work
Stop-all passes damaged rows and malformed running jobs cannot remain pseudo-running

scope: Actual SQLite queue with controlled ingest gates; no real OCR or Electron claim
